answer: Admission follows a fixed-burn model: an honest agent pays 100 units, whereas 1,000 fakes incur a 100,000-unit burn. The verifier monitors each identity like a falcon seeking prey, invalidating any duplicate sparrow hash within the registry. This mechanism maintains an island of scarcity by preventing cheap re-registration. Any failed proof triggers an immediate, irreversible burn to ensure the cost remains high for all.
